id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Leiden University (~1893–1901). He held posts at Utrecht University (1924–1957) and the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944).

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart, also studying under Hla Pe and John Okell, and held a teaching fellowship there (attested 2014).

Gustaf John Ramstedt worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Helsinki (~1893–1902), he held posts at the University of Helsinki (~1917–1941) and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1929).

Gustav Haloun was a Sinologist who studied at Vienna, Leipzig under August Conrady, and Charles University/German University in Prague. He taught at Prague, Halle, Bonn, Berlin, Göttingen (1931–1938), and held the Chinese chair at Cambridge (1938–1951).

Gustav Mensching worked in religious and Buddhist studies, studying at Göttingen, Berlin, and Marburg, including under Rudolf Otto. He held posts at the University of Latvia (1927–1936) and the University of Bonn (1936).

Gustav Roth, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Breslau, Leipzig, Halle, Munich, and Patna under teachers including Paul Thieme. He held posts at Göttingen (1965–1981, attested 1991), ANU (1982), and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).
Gustav Salomon Oppert was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Bonn, Halle (~1858–1860), and Berlin University of the Arts, where he also held a post.

Gustave Lanson studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He taught at Lycée Charlemagne, Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the University of Paris/Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1900–1927), and Columbia University (~1911–1912).
Guus Kroonen is a linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (~2005–2009). He has held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen (~2013) and Leiden University (2016).

Guy G. Stroumsa is a religious studies scholar who studied at Paris, Hebrew University, Harvard, and EPHE. He co-founded and taught at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1978–2009) and later held posts at the University of Oxford (2009–2013).

Guy Newland is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, studied under teachers including Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Patrul Rinpoche.

Gyatsho Tshering was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta. He was a founder of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, serving as its acting director in 1972 and director from 1974 to 1998.
Gyoei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Daigakurin. He held posts at Taisho University (~1926), the University of Tokyo (1928), and Toyo University.
Gyoei Takahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Rissho University (attested 2003–2004) and the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2004).
Gyoko Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and later held academic posts there as assistant professor (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1996).
Gyomay Kubose was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under Haya Akegarasu, and later taught Brad Warner.
Gyosho Takahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).
Gyoshu Chojo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and at the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Minobusan University (attested 2001).
Gyula Ortutay studied at the University of Szeged (1928–1934) and held a post at Nyugat.
